plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective line drawing of a rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field. The coil appears as a tall rectangular loop of several stacked turns, rendered as a striped gray band so the windings show, and tilted so its face is seen obliquely. A vertical axis labeled z passes through the coil's center, solid above and below the loop and dashed where it crosses the interior; a small circular arrow curls around its top to give the sense of rotation. A second axis labeled x runs diagonally toward the lower left, with a dashed segment continuing to the upper right. From the center point, a bold blue arrow labeled B points horizontally to the right as the uniform field, while an orange arrow labeled n-hat, the unit normal to the coil's surface, springs from the same origin and tilts down and to the right; a thin arc between the two marks the angle theta. Anchoring n-hat and B at a shared origin makes the angle between them the one quantity the reader tracks as the loop turns. The arrangement sets up the flux through a rotating coil and the emf that rotation induces.

vertical z-axis through the coil center, solid above and below the loop, dashed through the interior, labeled 'z' at top
small circular arrow curling around the top of the z-axis indicating rotation direction
x-axis running diagonally toward the lower left, labeled 'x', with a dashed continuation to the upper right
bold blue arrow labeled 'B' from the center pointing horizontally to the right (uniform field)
orange arrow labeled 'n̂' from the same center origin, the unit normal to the coil plane, initially tilted down and to the right
thin arc between B and n̂ labeled 'θ' marking the angle between them
flux readout Φ = BA cos(θ) near the figure
graph view: time axes with synchronized sinusoidal flux Φ(t) and induced emf ε(t) traces (emf shifted 90°)

interactions.label: Coil angle θ
interactions.teaches: Rotating the coil about the z-axis sweeps n̂ relative to B; the flux readout Φ = BA cos θ shows that only the field component through the coil's area contributes to magnetic flux

interactions.label: Steady rotation
interactions.teaches: Watching the coil spin at constant angular speed while flux and induced emf traces update together shows that alternating emf arises from the continuously changing angle between n̂ and B

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching between the 3D coil diagram and the synchronized Φ(t) and ε(t) curves connects the geometric angle in the picture to the sinusoidal quantities used in the calculation

demo_steps.title: Maximum flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 0 the normal n̂ aligns with B, the coil face is fully open to the field, and the flux readout shows its maximum Φ = BA.

demo_steps.title: Zero flux
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 90° the coil is edge-on to B, no field lines pass through the loop, and Φ = 0 — even though the field is unchanged.

demo_steps.title: From geometry to graph
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the graph view: with θ = 45° the marker sits partway down the cosine flux curve, linking the picture's angle to the plotted quantity.

demo_steps.title: Steady rotation and alternating emf
demo_steps.narration: Play the rotation: flux traces a cosine while the induced emf traces a sine (largest where flux crosses zero), showing how alternating emf is generated.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Coil: rectangle ~2.4 wide × 3.6 tall world units, built from 4-5 nested rectangular loops (TubeGeometry or thin boxes) to suggest stacked turns, striped light gray #c8c8c8 / #a8a8a8. Coil center at origin; rotation axis is the vertical z-axis. z-axis: black line from y=-2.6 to y=+2.6, dashed segment through the coil interior, 'z' label at top; small curved arrow (radius ~0.4) around the axis at y≈2.2. x-axis: black line from origin toward lower-left to (-2.4,-1.2,-1.2)-ish in screen terms (world (-2.2, 0, +2.2) toward camera-left), dashed continuation to upper right. B arrow: bold blue #1a66cc, from origin along +X_screen (world direction fixed, e.g. (1,0,0) perpendicular to the initial coil normal offset), length ~2.2, labeled 'B'. n̂ arrow: orange #e08000, length ~1.6, initially 45° below/right of B (θ=45), labeled 'n̂'. θ arc: thin curve of radius ~0.7 between B and n̂. n̂ is the coil plane normal: as θ changes the whole coil rotates about the z-axis and n̂ rotates with it. Flux: Φ = BA cos θ; emf: ε = NBA ω sin(ωt) with B=A=N=1 for the graph; graph view plots Φ(t)=cos(ωt) and ε(t)=sin(ωt) over 0–2 periods with a moving marker synced to the animation.
interactionPlan.notes: Three.js: rotate a single coil group about the world Y (z in figure labels) axis; keep B fixed in world space and recompute the θ arc and flux readout each frame. During animation, drive the same rotation with ω and advance the graph marker in sync. Toggle shows/hides the 3D scene vs. a 2D plot overlay rather than rebuilding geometry. Use dashed LineDashedMaterial for the axis segments passing through the coil.

authoredContext:
A Rectangular Coil Rotating in a Magnetic Field A rectangular coil of area A and N turns is placed in a uniform magnetic field B→=Bj^, as shown in the figure. The coil is rotated about the z-axis through its center at a constant angular velocity ω. Obtain an expression for the induced emf in the coil.

A rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field.

Figure shows a rectangular coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field.

Strategy According to the diagram, the angle between the perpendicular to the surface (n^) and the magnetic field (B→) is θ. The dot product of B→·n^ simplifies to only the cosθ component of the magnetic field, namely where the magnetic field projects onto the unit area vector n^. The magnitude of the magnetic field and the area of the loop are fixed over time, which makes the integration simplify quickly. The induced emf is written out using Faraday’s law.
